summary: This lecture tells of the grandfather and forefathers of the Prophet ﷺ who shaped Mecca before his birth. The ustaz explains how Hashim, a far-sighted man, turned poor Mecca into a world trading hub through the ilaf agreements and two seasons of trade journeys, as recorded in Surah Quraysh. Then the story of his son Shaybah, called Abdul Muttalib, the rediscovery of the well of Zamzam, the vow to sacrifice a son who was ransomed with a hundred camels, and Abdullah's marriage to Aminah. The ustaz stresses that all of this was Allah preparing the stage for the birth of the final Prophet.
keyPoints: The Prophet's ﷺ lineage that is certainly authentic goes only as far as Adnan; after that, back to Prophet Adam, it is not known for certain.
Mecca used to be poor because it had no trade route, until Hashim opened trade agreements with tribes and great powers.
Surah Quraysh records the effort of ilaf and the winter and summer journeys that transformed Mecca's economy.
Shaybah was called Abdul Muttalib because he was mistaken for a slave of his uncle, Al-Muttalib.
Abdul Muttalib rediscovered Zamzam and held its ownership, which strengthened his family's political standing.
The vow to sacrifice a son, who was ransomed with a hundred camels, is the origin of the blood money of a hundred camels in the Shariah.
Hashim, Abdul Muttalib and Abdullah were Allah's preparation for the birth of the Prophet ﷺ.

chapters.title: Introduction: the Prophet's ﷺ lineage
chapters.summary: The ustaz opens the episode and explains how far the Prophet's ﷺ lineage can be established.

chapters.title: Three figures and Fihr's political reform
chapters.summary: A focus on Hashim, Abdul Muttalib and Abdullah, after Fihr seized power from Khuza'ah.

chapters.title: A poor Mecca
chapters.summary: Mecca was visited only in the Hajj season and its people lived in extreme poverty.

chapters.title: The geopolitics of Rome and Persia
chapters.summary: Hashim thought about how to revive Mecca amid the clash of two great powers.

chapters.title: World trade routes
chapters.summary: Goods from Africa and India went up to Yemen, while silk and other goods came from the north.

chapters.title: The old wealth of South Asia
chapters.summary: The ustaz mentions the wealth of India and Bangladesh before colonisation, and their merchants' support for Mecca.

chapters.title: Ilaf and Surah Quraysh
chapters.summary: Hashim made trade agreements, and this effort is recorded in Surah Quraysh.

chapters.title: Mecca becomes a trading hub
chapters.summary: Two seasons of journeys turned Mecca into the richest town, and Hashim fed the pilgrims with crumbled bread.

chapters.title: Hashim, Salma and Gaza
chapters.summary: Hashim married Salma in Yathrib and died in Gaza.

chapters.title: Shaybah becomes Abdul Muttalib
chapters.summary: Salma kept her child's birth secret, then Al-Muttalib brought him to Mecca and he became known as Abdul Muttalib.

chapters.title: The rediscovery of Zamzam
chapters.summary: Abdul Muttalib dreamed he should dig Zamzam, and found it despite objections from other tribes.

chapters.title: The vow and the hundred camels
chapters.summary: Abdul Muttalib vowed to sacrifice a son, and Abdullah was ransomed with a hundred camels.

chapters.title: Abdullah and Aminah
chapters.summary: Abdullah was married to Aminah, and Abdul Muttalib married Hala; Abdullah later died on the way home.

chapters.title: Closing: Surah Ali Imran 67 and 68
chapters.summary: The ustaz closes with verses about Prophet Ibrahim and those closest to him.

lessons.title: Lineage does not decide the Hereafter
lessons.body: Noble lineage is indeed seen as a high standing, but it does not decide one's fate in the Hereafter.

lessons.title: Claiming to follow without acting
lessons.body: Many claim to follow someone but do not do what he taught; the people of Mecca knew Prophet Ibrahim but had strayed.

lessons.title: Think far and long term
lessons.body: Hashim saw opportunity beyond poverty with far-sightedness and long-term strategy.

lessons.title: Use your strategic position
lessons.body: Mecca's place in the middle of the trade routes was used to make it a world business hub.

lessons.title: Share wealth
lessons.body: When Mecca became rich, Hashim shared with the pilgrims, and this is the origin of the title Hashim.

lessons.title: Understand the geopolitical background of the sirah
lessons.body: The clash of Rome and Persia is a background that affected the course of the sirah, including Surah Ar-Rum.

lessons.title: The wheel of history turns
lessons.body: Regions that were once richest can become poor, and vice versa; today's conditions are not permanent.

lessons.title: Family ties shaped the sirah
lessons.body: Who supported and who cancelled the boycott, and how the Prophet was allowed back into Mecca, were tied to family relationships.

lessons.title: The Hijra to the maternal family's town
lessons.body: Madinah is the town of the Prophet's ancestors on the female side, and Allah designed it from the beginning.

lessons.title: Illiteracy at that time was a strength
lessons.body: In the Arab context then, those who wrote were seen as weak because they did not memorise; it is also a sign of intelligence.

lessons.title: Keeping promises
lessons.body: The Arabs did not break their word once spoken, and Abdul Muttalib was earnest in fulfilling his vow.

dalil.context: The ustaz rejects posters that extend the lineage directly to Prophet Adam.
dalil.translation: The Prophet's ﷺ lineage that can be established goes up to Adnan, and it is mentioned in Sahih Bukhari. After Ismail back to Prophet Adam it is not known for certain.

dalil.context: The ustaz states lineage does not decide the Hereafter, but considering it is not a negative thing.
dalil.translation: The Prophet ﷺ mentioned that among the things considered in choosing a spouse is lineage.

dalil.context: The ustaz reads Surah Quraysh as a record of Hashim's effort to open trade agreements.
dalil.translation: [He did this] to make the Quraysh feel secure,

dalil.context: This verse mentions ilaf and the winter and summer journeys.
dalil.translation: secure in their winter and summer journeys.

dalil.context: The command to worship the Lord of this House, the Kaaba.
dalil.translation: So let them worship the Lord of this House:

dalil.context: Allah fed them against hunger and made them safe from fear.
dalil.translation: who provides them with food to ward off hunger, safety to ward off fear.

dalil.context: The ustaz explains the context: silk was very expensive and a symbol of luxury and pride.
dalil.translation: The Prophet ﷺ forbade silk for men except for those suffering a skin disease.

dalil.context: Prophet Ibrahim was neither a Jew nor a Christian, but an upright Muslim on tawhid.
dalil.translation: Abraham was neither a Jew nor a Christian. He was upright and devoted to God, never an idolater,

dalil.context: The people closest to Prophet Ibrahim are his followers, Prophet Muhammad ﷺ and the believers.
dalil.translation: and the people who are closest to him are those who truly follow his ways, this Prophet, and [true] believers- God is close to [true] believers.

sirah.era: Before the Prophet's ﷺ birth: his ancestors in Mecca
sirah.summary: This episode traces the three closest figures before the Prophet's ﷺ birth, Hashim, Abdul Muttalib and Abdullah, and how Mecca's economy, politics and religion were shaped.

events.label: Birth of Shaybah

events.desc: After Hashim died, the child was named Shaybah and brought to Mecca by Al-Muttalib.

events.label: Zamzam

events.desc: After four days of dreams, he dug and found the water of Zamzam, and held its ownership.

events.desc: The azlam arrows determined the ransom until it reached a hundred camels.

events.label: Marriage

events.desc: Abdullah married Aminah and Abdul Muttalib married Hala; Abdullah died when the Prophet ﷺ was two months in the womb.
